python -c "
import json
from dspy.adapters.types.tool import ToolCalls

# Case 1: canonical dict with tool_calls key
data = {'tool_calls': [{'name': 'foo', 'args': {'a': 1}}, {'name': 'bar', 'args': {'b': 2}}]}
r = ToolCalls.validate_input(data)
print('canonical:', r)
assert r == {'tool_calls': [{'name': 'foo', 'args': {'a': 1}}, {'name': 'bar', 'args': {'b': 2}}]}

# Case 2: single object without tool_calls
data = {'name': 'foo', 'args': {'a': 1}}
r = ToolCalls.validate_input(data)
print('single obj:', r)
assert r == {'tool_calls': [{'name': 'foo', 'args': {'a': 1}}]}

# Case 3: bare list
data = [{'name': 'foo', 'args': {'a': 1}}, {'name': 'bar', 'args': {'b': 2}}]
r = ToolCalls.validate_input(data)
print('bare list:', r)
assert r == {'tool_calls': [{'name': 'foo', 'args': {'a': 1}}, {'name': 'bar', 'args': {'b': 2}}]}

# Case 4: JSON string of canonical
r = ToolCalls.validate_input(json.dumps({'tool_calls': [{'name': 'foo', 'args': {'a': 1}}]}))
print('json canonical:', r)
assert r == {'tool_calls': [{'name': 'foo', 'args': {'a': 1}}]}

# Case 5: JSON string of single object
r = ToolCalls.validate_input(json.dumps({'name': 'foo', 'args': {'a': 1}}))
print('json single obj:', r)
assert r == {'tool_calls': [{'name': 'foo', 'args': {'a': 1}}]}

# Case 6: JSON string of bare list
r = ToolCalls.validate_input(json.dumps([{'name': 'foo', 'args': {'a': 1}}]))
print('json bare list:', r)
assert r == {'tool_calls': [{'name': 'foo', 'args': {'a': 1}}]}

# Case 7: non-JSON string returns unchanged
r = ToolCalls.validate_input('not a json string')
print('non-json:', repr(r))
assert r == 'not a json string'

# Case 8: invalid JSON that starts with { 
r = ToolCalls.validate_input('{broken json')
print('broken json:', repr(r))
assert r == '{broken json'

# Case 9: full construction works
tc = ToolCalls(tool_calls=[{'name': 'foo', 'args': {'a': 1}}])
print('constructed:', tc)
print('format:', tc.format())

print('ALL PASSED')
"

from dspy.adapters.types.tool import ToolCalls

# Constructing directly from a bare list (should now normalize via the before validator)
tc = ToolCalls([{'name': 'foo', 'args': {'a': 1}}])
print('from list:', tc.tool_calls)

# Constructing from a single object
tc = ToolCalls({'name': 'foo', 'args': {'a': 1}})

# from_dict_list still works

"

python -c "
from dspy.adapters.types.tool import ToolCalls

# Normalization via the field value (realistic: signature output field is set to raw LM data)
# Pass a bare list as the tool_calls field value
tc = ToolCalls(tool_calls=[{'name': 'foo', 'args': {'a': 1}}])
print('tool_calls field list:', tc.tool_calls)

# The before-validator path is what validate_input exercises. Confirm a normalized dict
# passed through validate_input then used to construct works.
normalized = ToolCalls.validate_input({'name': 'foo', 'args': {'a': 1}})
tc = ToolCalls(**normalized)
print('via validate_input single obj:', tc.tool_calls)

normalized = ToolCalls.validate_input([{'name': 'foo', 'args': {'a': 1}}])
tc = ToolCalls(**normalized)
print('via validate_input bare list:', tc.tool_calls)
print('OK')
"
